solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Sailor by old platform covers wreck (8)

indicatorNotes.covers: the platform wraps itself round the sailor and the old

blocks.note: a stage is a raised platform; it goes round AB + O

annotation.surface: A sailor on an old platform looks on at a shipwreck.
annotation.walkthrough: "Wreck" looks like a noun to go with the sailor, but it is the verb: to sabotage something is to wreck it.
annotation.definitionFit: To sabotage a plan or machine is to wreck it deliberately.

entries.clue: One abandoning capital for surfing destination? (4)

indicatorNotes.abandoning: the one leaves the capital, so the I is removed

blocks.note: one = I, the letter that walks out
the capital of Bulgaria, with its I taken away

annotation.surface: Someone quits a capital city to go surfing at the beach.
annotation.walkthrough: The surfing is channel-surfing, flicking through TV channels, which you do from the sofa, not on a wave.
annotation.definitionFit: The sofa is where a couch potato sits to surf TV channels, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Mature bird demolished fish in main area (7,8)

indicatorNotes.demolished: the letters of MATURE BIRD are knocked down and rebuilt

annotation.surface: An old bird is destroyed by fish somewhere at sea.
annotation.walkthrough: "Main" is the old poetic word for the open sea, so a "main area" is a stretch of ocean.
annotation.definitionFit: Main is the poetic word for the open sea, and this stretch of the western Atlantic is famous for vanished ships and planes.

entries.clue: Child completely stone cold finally came to (8)

indicatorNotes.finally: take the final letter of each of stone and cold

blocks.note: a tot is a small child

annotation.surface: A child knocked out stone cold finally regains consciousness.
annotation.walkthrough: "Came to" pretends to mean woke up after being knocked out; here it is what a bill does when it came to fifty pounds.
annotation.definitionFit: A bill that came to a sum totalled that sum.

entries.clue: Labour good for Charlie in shipping? (5)

indicatorNotes.for: G stands in for C, as one player comes on for another

blocks.note: craft = ships; its C (Charlie in the NATO alphabet) comes out, leaving RAFT

annotation.surface: A political question about whether Labour is good for the shipping industry.
annotation.walkthrough: Labour is not the British political party here, just hard work. Graft is British slang for hard work.
annotation.definitionFit: Graft, in British usage, is hard work, so labour.

entries.clue: Rod starts to import US Motown and soft metal (6)

indicatorNotes.starts to: take the starting letter of each following word

annotation.surface: Rod starts importing American Motown records and soft metal music.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Rod Stewart and music genres; "soft metal" is quite literal.
annotation.definitionFit: Barium is a soft, silvery alkaline-earth metal.

entries.clue: Trap contingent of westbound French submarines (6)

indicatorNotes.contingent of: a contingent is a part of a larger group, so the answer is a part of the words
indicatorNotes.westbound: in the across direction west is leftward, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of frencH into SUBMArines

annotation.surface: A group of French submarines heads west to set a trap.
annotation.walkthrough: "Westbound" is an across-clue reversal word used in a down clue; it still just means read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: as a verb, to lie in wait and spring on someone is to trap them.

entries.clue: Popular pieces in parade followed by high profile player (15)

indicatorNotes.in: the pieces go inside the parade

blocks.note: to parade is to strut; it goes round MEN
the A-list are the most famous people

annotation.surface: A popular item in a parade is followed by a famous player.
annotation.walkthrough: Pieces are chessmen, a common crossword source of MEN.
annotation.definitionFit: An instrumentalist plays a musical instrument, so is a player.

entries.clue: Reported behaviour on hot river residence (5,5)

indicatorNotes.Reported: what is heard, not seen, so MANNER is heard as MANOR

blocks.note: manner = behaviour; said aloud it matches MANOR
H = hot, as on a tap
the Ouse is a river in England

annotation.surface: A report on someone's behaviour on a hot river.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a crossword favourite among English rivers.
annotation.definitionFit: A manor house is the main residence of a country estate.

entries.clue: Sticking Bill in this location with conservationists (8)

blocks.note: NT = National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

annotation.surface: Someone sticks a bill up here with the approval of conservationists.
annotation.walkthrough: "With" simply joins NT on the end. Adherent is used here as the adjective meaning sticking fast.
annotation.definitionFit: Adherent as an adjective means sticking, adhering.

entries.clue: Direct Henry feeding bear behind tree (5-4)

indicatorNotes.feeding: H goes into STAND like food into a mouth
indicatorNotes.behind: what stands behind a tree comes after it in the line of reading, so STAND follows FIR

blocks.note: H = henry, the unit of inductance
to bear something is to stand it; H goes inside

annotation.surface: An instruction to put Henry feeding a bear behind a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bear" is the verb, as in "I can't stand it".
annotation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives for experience gained yourself, with no go-between: a direct account is one from the source.

entries.clue: Not one close family member recalled plain beasts (5)

blocks.note: no = not one, as in 'no sheep'

annotation.surface: Not one close relative remembered the ordinary animals.
annotation.walkthrough: "Plain" looks like "ordinary" but means the Great Plains, where bison roam.
annotation.definitionFit: Bison are the beasts of the North American plains.

entries.clue: Con stealer of chips that are not digitally secured? (4)

annotation.definition2: stealer of chips that are not digitally secured?

blocks.note: con as a verb: to fool or swindle someone

blocks.clueFragment: stealer of chips that are not digitally secured?
blocks.note: seagulls snatch chips from people not holding them tightly

annotation.surface: A con artist steals poker chips that are not locked by digital security.
annotation.walkthrough: "Digitally" means with the fingers, not electronically, and the chips are fried ones at the British seaside, where gulls grab them.
annotation.definitionFit: To gull is to dupe, and the seaside gull steals chips from loose hands.

entries.clue: Three had regularly selected more reliable fund manager (9)

indicatorNotes.regularly selected: letters picked at a regular interval, every other one

annotation.surface: Three people chose a more reliable fund manager.
annotation.walkthrough: The alternate letters run across the two words as if they were one: ThReE hAd.
annotation.definitionFit: A treasurer manages the funds of a club or society.

entries.clue: Quiet about Hearts supporter that’s raised goal record? (10)

indicatorNotes.about: about in its sense of around, so the quiet SH is wrapped round CORES
indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raising a word turns it upside down, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: a core is a heart, as of an apple
a golf tee supports the ball; it is raised, so it reads upwards

annotation.surface: A Hearts football fan has quietly raised a record of the goals.
annotation.walkthrough: Hearts is a Scottish football club, which makes the surface about football; in the wordplay it is just CORES.
annotation.definitionFit: A scoresheet records the goals, hence the question mark on a slightly loose definition.

entries.clue: Spanish man turned on male English shepherds (10)

indicatorNotes.turned: turned round, so SENOR reads backwards
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, placed after the rest

blocks.note: señor is Spanish for a man, Mr; turned, it reads backwards

annotation.surface: A Spanish man turns against the English male shepherds.
annotation.walkthrough: "Shepherds" is a verb here: to guide or look after.
annotation.definitionFit: To chaperone someone is to shepherd them, keeping an eye on them.

entries.clue: Port boys periodically manage device used in canal (8)

indicatorNotes.periodically: at regular intervals, so every other letter

blocks.note: the even letters of pOrT bOyS

annotation.surface: Boys in a port occasionally handle a gadget used on a canal.
annotation.walkthrough: The canal is the ear canal, not a waterway.
annotation.definitionFit: An otoscope is the instrument a doctor uses to look into the ear canal.

entries.clue: Skinned meat items maybe loaded into barrel (4)

indicatorNotes.Skinned: skin removed, so the outer letters go

blocks.note: GAMMON, cured ham, without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Skinned cuts of meat are stuffed into a barrel.
annotation.walkthrough: Gammon is British cured ham. The barrel is a gun's barrel.
annotation.definitionFit: Ammo, bullets and shells, is what is loaded into a gun barrel.

entries.clue: Vicar cutting cold fool last of the crack (8)

indicatorNotes.cutting: REV cuts into the letters that follow it

annotation.surface: A vicar interrupts a cold fool at the last of the joke.
annotation.walkthrough: "Crack" looks like a joke to go with the fool, but it is a fissure. Rev. is short for Reverend, the title of a vicar.
annotation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep crack, especially in a glacier.

entries.clue: Two military units seldom seen (4)

annotation.surface: Two army units are hardly ever spotted.
annotation.walkthrough: The Royal Artillery and Royal Engineers are British Army corps, standard crossword abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rare bird is one that is seldom seen.

entries.clue: Tracks profit on renovated street in recession (10)

indicatorNotes.renovated: made over, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.in recession: going backwards, so ST reads TS

blocks.note: ST = street, in recession so it goes backwards

annotation.surface: An economic piece: profit tracked on a renovated street during a recession.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is financial news; "Tracks" is the plural noun, the marks left by feet.
annotation.definitionFit: Tracks as a plural noun: the marks left in mud or snow, which a tracker follows.

entries.clue: Minister beat ten defenceless guards (6)

indicatorNotes.guards: the words hold the answer inside them

annotation.surface: A government minister has beaten ten helpless security guards.
annotation.walkthrough: "Minister" is the verb, to minister to someone, not a politician.
annotation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean looking after someone's needs, as a nurse does for a patient.

entries.clue: Epic fight with cross characters holding clubs (9)

indicatorNotes.holding: to hold something is to have it within your grasp, so TAUS closes round C

blocks.note: tau is the Greek letter T, shaped like a cross
C = clubs, the card suit; it goes inside TAUS

annotation.surface: An epic fight between people who are cross.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cross characters" sounds like angry people but means letters shaped like a cross.
annotation.definitionFit: Spartacus is the 1960 Kubrick epic film about the gladiator revolt.

entries.clue: Jack briefly working for place that may fix locks (5)

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a jack (tar) is a sailor, a SALT; it loses its T

annotation.surface: Jack briefly works for a locksmith.
annotation.walkthrough: The locks are locks of hair, not door locks, so the place is a hair salon.
annotation.definitionFit: A hair salon fixes locks of hair.

entries.clue: Container lorry’s first on road heading for Rome? (4)

indicatorNotes.first: take the opening letter of lorry
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, placed after VIA

blocks.note: via is Latin for road, as in Via Appia

annotation.surface: A container lorry drives on the road to Rome.
annotation.walkthrough: The road is one in Rome, a Latin via; a lorry is a British truck.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: the small glass bottle for medicine or scent is one kind of container.

entries.clue: Visit capsized vessels avoiding half of loch (4)

indicatorNotes.capsized: turned upside down, so in a down clue the word reads backwards
indicatorNotes.avoiding: to avoid something is to steer clear of it, so the CH is left out
indicatorNotes.half of: the second half of LOCH is CH

blocks.note: yachts are vessels; capsized, they read upwards
the back half of loCH, the letters to be avoided

annotation.surface: A visit to boats that overturned on a Scottish lake.
annotation.walkthrough: A loch is a Scottish lake, fitting the capsized vessels.
annotation.definitionFit: As verbs, both mean spending time as a guest, as with relatives over the holidays.

entries.clue: Joy almost goes after exposed lean bird (5)

indicatorNotes.goes after: to go after is to follow, so the shortened joy comes after the stripped lean
indicatorNotes.exposed: stripped of its outside, so the outer letters go

blocks.note: GLEE, joy, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Joy almost vanishes after exposing a thin bird.
annotation.walkthrough: "Lean" is the word to be stripped, not the bird's shape.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the eagle is one bird among many.

entries.clue: Top car son struck with king aboard (4,5)

indicatorNotes.aboard: a passenger aboard is inside the vehicle, so the king R sits inside HIT

blocks.note: the Volkswagen Polo is a car
R = rex, king; it goes inside HIT

annotation.surface: A top car has hit a son with the king on board.
annotation.walkthrough: "Top" looks like an adjective, best, but it is the garment.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the collared short-sleeved shirt is one kind of top, the garment worn on the upper body.

entries.clue: Walks from hotel leaving clothing (6)

indicatorNotes.leaving: the hotel leaves, walking out of the clothing word, so its H is dropped

blocks.note: H = hotel in the NATO alphabet, the letter to go
slang for clothes, the word for strands of cotton, minus its H

annotation.surface: Someone walks out of a hotel leaving their clothes behind.
annotation.walkthrough: "Threads" is slang for clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb form: to tread a path is to walk it, as in 'treads the boards'.

entries.clue: Experts carrying pole attempt descent (8)

indicatorNotes.carrying: to carry something is to hold it within, so ACES has N inside

blocks.note: N = north pole; it goes inside ACES

annotation.surface: Experts carrying a pole attempt to climb down.
annotation.walkthrough: "Descent" looks like climbing down but means lineage.
annotation.definitionFit: Your descent is your ancestry, the line you come from.
